\section{Purpose and result vocabulary}
\label{sec:eng-purpose}

This specification turns the shared SCI-JINC authority into a future
conformance-review surface and introduces no independent science.  If this
engineering prose is broader than the shared modules, the shared module
controls.  A future result is exactly \emph{pass}, \emph{fail}, \emph{not
assessed}, or \emph{not applicable under an explicit contract-authorized
condition}.  Missing evidence is never pass.

The conformance object is one claimed realization under one exact contract,
source packet, observation, array, plan, coefficient family, parameter set,
target WCS, destination, numerical profile, certificate, and lifecycle
generation.  These identities must be bound before any conclusion.

\section{Applicability and fail-closed inputs}
\label{sec:eng-applicability}

A numerical route requires mutually compatible exact bindings for:

\begin{enumerate}
\item the transformed occurrence and same-processed-sample AST coordinate;
\item one registered, selected, realized PTC family that explicitly permits
SCI-JINC, with payload, QC, generation, and source identity;
\item one owner-authorized TolTEC array parameter set;
\item one positive-integer phase count selected by the accepted request or one
exact owner-authorized versioned mode policy;
\item one compatible target WCS and positive sample frequency; and
\item one exact numerical profile and matching certificate when numerical
adequacy or near-cancellation support is claimed.
\end{enumerate}

The coefficient family/payload, TolTEC parameter set, numerical profile, and
certificate are not admitted or supplied by this source packet.  Their routes
are typed unavailable.  Unity, ordinary-MAP permission, another family, an
inherited 45~m denominator, inherited shape values, mode-dependent
$r_{\max}$, an ambient phase count, or any implementation default cannot
repair them.

\section{Exact discrete reference oracle}
\label{sec:eng-oracle}

The oracle evaluates the midpoint-quantized discrete operator in exact real
arithmetic.  There is no hidden continuous-phase or pixel-area-integrated
target.

For $\mathcal D=\{1,\ldots,N_x\}\times\{1,\ldots,N_y\}$ and exact AST coordinate
$\boldsymbol u_i$, resolve componentwise
\[
 c_{i\mu}=\lfloor u_{i\mu}+\tfrac12\rfloor,\qquad
 \phi_{i\mu}=u_{i\mu}-c_{i\mu}\in[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12).
\]
The owner-approved positive-axis half tie selects the larger integer.  For
$n_{\mathrm{sub}}=\texttt{subpixel\_n}\in\mathbb N_{>0}$,
\[
 q_{i\mu}=\lfloor n_{\mathrm{sub}}(\phi_{i\mu}+\tfrac12)\rfloor,\qquad
 \widehat\phi_{i\mu}=-\tfrac12+
 \frac{q_{i\mu}+\tfrac12}{n_{\mathrm{sub}}}.
\]
Bins are left closed and right open, and an interior-boundary tie selects the
upper bin.  No parity restriction exists.  With even $n_{\mathrm{sub}}$, exact
$\phi=0$ maps to $+1/(2n_{\mathrm{sub}})$.  Owner-approved disposition A
retains this rule for every positive $n_{\mathrm{sub}}$ with no zero-phase
special case.  WCS axis order and orientation are
normative.  The logical cache key is
$(q_{i1},q_{i2},d_1,d_2)$; storage may differ only by a proven
value-preserving bijection.

The complete target WCS binds frame, projection, reference values, one-based
reference pixel, dimensions, units, axis order/signs, rotation, handedness,
version, and constant pixel matrix $\mathbf M$, with
\[
 \mathbf M^{\mathsf T}\mathbf M=\Delta^2\mathbf I,\qquad\Delta>0.
\]
Arbitrary recorded rotation or reflection is permitted.  Skewed or
anisotropic geometry is incompatible; a scalar size cannot conceal it.

For array $a$,
\[
 h_a=\left\lceil s_a(r_{\max})_a/\Delta\right\rceil,\qquad
 \boldsymbol d\in\{-h_a,\ldots,+h_a\}^2.
\]
An occurrence with $\boldsymbol c_i\notin\mathcal D$ contributes nowhere.
Otherwise set
$\boldsymbol p=\boldsymbol c_i+\boldsymbol d$ and retain it exactly when
$\boldsymbol p\in\mathcal D$.  There is no circular cutoff, wrap, reflection,
completion, or edge renormalization.  At the destination pixel centre,
\[
 \widehat r_{i\boldsymbol d}=
 \lVert\mathbf M(\boldsymbol d-\widehat{\boldsymbol\phi}_i)\rVert_2,\qquad
 \widehat r'_{i\boldsymbol d}=\widehat r_{i\boldsymbol d}/s_a.
\]
The exact second-factor root is
$j_{1,1}=\min\{x>0:J_1(x)=0\}$; a rounded decimal is nonnormative.  The shared
kernel and estimator equations then control.  Outer rows and corners remain
evaluated beyond the first-zero radius.

For an exact integer-center occurrence with even $n_{\mathrm{sub}}$, zero
phase on both axes and $\boldsymbol d=\boldsymbol0$ shall give
\[
 \widehat r_{i\boldsymbol0}=\frac{\Delta}{\sqrt{2}n_{\mathrm{sub}}},
 \qquad
 \kappa_{i,\boldsymbol c_i}=\kappa_a\!\left(
 \frac{\Delta}{\sqrt{2}n_{\mathrm{sub}}s_a};
 a_a,b_a,c_a,(r_{\max})_a\right).
\]
The expected coefficient is the exact nonzero-radius oracle value, not an
imposed $\kappa_a(0)=1$.

\section{Numerical profile and certificate}
\label{sec:eng-numerical-profile}

Algebraic support requires finite inputs and exact discrete coefficients,
$Q_p>0$, and $C_p\ne0$.  Numerical adequacy separately requires the complete
pair below.

\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.24\textwidth}
                        >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.66\textwidth}@{}}
\caption{Profile-plus-certificate checklist.}\label{tab:eng-profile}\\
\toprule
Field & Required exact content \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Field & Required exact content \\
\midrule
\endhead
Profile identity & Owner, identifier, version, source digest, compatibility,
lifecycle, and supersession. \\
Observable and error & Observable; absolute, relative, or mixed form;
reference norm/magnitude; units; numerator and denominator treatment. \\
Domain and aggregation & Exact source/parameter/pixel domain and simultaneous,
componentwise, or worst-case interpretation. \\
Near-zero and inequality & Exact zero/near-zero rule and one exact pass/fail
inequality, without a qualitative fidelity substitute. \\
Certificate method & Exact oracle, bound/comparison method, uncertainty
semantics, and authorized coverage. \\
Certificate binding & Candidate, source bytes, observation/array, coefficient
generation, parameters, WCS, phase count, destination, reduction policy,
profile, lifecycle, and immutable certificate identity. \\
Certificate result & Exact bounds, exceptions, and pass/fail over the complete
declared domain. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

If $|\widehat C_p-C_p|\le\epsilon_{C,p}$ is certified, normalized support
requires $|\widehat C_p|>\epsilon_{C,p}$.  Otherwise zero remains inside the
certified denominator interval.  The profile must provide any additional
map-error inequality.  A profile alone, certificate alone, successful run,
two agreeing realizations, or finite nonzero machine result is not a pass.

A passing pair establishes only finite-precision fidelity to the exact
selected discrete SCI-JINC oracle on its declared domain.  It does not
establish parameter or phase-count adequacy, square-truncation adequacy,
source-response or beam fidelity, photometric or astrometric performance,
optimality, observational validation, response/covariance fidelity,
readiness, or production authority.  TolTEC parameter-set qualification is a
separate scientific and observational program.

No exact owner-approved profile or matching certificate is admitted or
supplied.  Numerical adequacy and near-cancellation support are therefore
\textbf{typed unavailable}, not tested, failed, or achieved.

\section{Compact generative replay}
\label{sec:eng-replay}

A future assessor shall:

\begin{enumerate}
\item verify all source bytes and bind requested, effective, resolved, and
realized contract, plan, observation, array, destination, and lifecycle;
\item reconstruct the occurrence population from immutable PTC/AST parents
and JINC upstream-occurrence admission under its exact Registry identity;
\item bind coefficient permission/generation/payload/QC, parameter set, WCS
metric, phase count, and sample frequency;
\item reapply the owner-approved upper-bin lattice and positive-axis tie,
bins, midpoints, square extent, centre gate,
edge crop, and point-centre radius;
\item evaluate the exact discrete kernel and coupled $N_p$, $C_p$, $Q_p$,
$m_p$, and $T_p^{(\kappa^2)}$ equations;
\item evaluate the exact profile/certificate and denominator separation;
\item verify five-role atomic publication, local versus whole failure, the
static prohibition on companion roles, completion, and lifecycle; and
\item compare regenerated identities and values under the profile's exact
relation, recording every mismatch without fallback.
\end{enumerate}

The compact generative record binds every item above, including source,
parentage, coefficient, parameter, WCS, geometry, cancellation,
profile/certificate, destination, ODQ-107 scope identity, exact-source lock,
required-role state, failure, and completion.  It contains no per-bundle response/covariance
information-state record.
It is plan/bundle lineage, not a generalized provenance product or dense
per-contribution archive.

\section{Future assessment and evidence}
\label{sec:eng-procedure}

A later assessor binds identity and applicability, executes the replay,
checks units, signs, limits, grouping, lifecycle, and five-role publication,
then evaluates all 44 requirements and 36 predictions.  Each record contains
construction, expected and observed results, evidence locator, exact
profile/tolerance authority, and result state.  Numerical assessment occurs
only when both profile and certificate are authorized and bound.

This is evidence ordering, not implementation architecture.  Compilation, a
source hash, one numerical example, or one stored product cannot establish
complete conformity.

\section{Output-role and claim discipline}
\label{sec:eng-claims}

The ODQ-107 schema remains exactly $N_p$, $C_p$, $Q_p$, derived $m_p$ with
local support, and $T_p^{(\kappa^2)}$.  $Q_p$ is not automatically precision;
$C_p$ is not exposure; coefficient-squared time is not acquired time.  Whole
role failure suppresses the bundle, while local cancellation or unavailable
support remains map content without a finite substitute.

Algebraic conformity, representation fidelity, response/covariance fidelity,
numerical validation, observational performance, readiness, and production
authorization are separate conclusions with separate evidence and authority.
At revision \DocumentRevision{}, no candidate was inspected and every later
claim is not assessed, not performed, or no claim.
